rows.note: Use 薯條 as the everyday all-purpose word for French fries.

example.english: I grabbed a fry to eat.
example.jyutping: ngo5 ling1 zo2 jat1 tiu4 syu4 tiu4 sik6

rows.note: Use 煎 as the all-purpose cooking verb for frying food in a pan, especially eggs or meat.

example.english: I used a wok to fry two eggs this morning.
example.traditional: 我朝早用鑊煎咗兩隻蛋。
example.jyutping: ngo5 ziu1 zou2 jung6 wok6 zin1 zo2 loeng5 zek3 daan6

rows.note: Use 炒 when the food is being stir-fried or tossed in oil over high heat.

example.english: I’m going to fry the beef over high heat tonight.
example.jyutping: ngo5 gam1 maan5 jung6 daai6 fo2 caau2 ngau4 juk6

rows.note: Use this for a fry-up meal of items such as sausages, bacon, and eggs.

example.english: We had an English fry for breakfast today.
example.traditional: 我哋今日早餐食英式早餐。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 gam1 jat6 zou2 caan1 sik6 jing1 sik1 zou2 caan1

rows.note: Use 燒壞 for frying an electronic component or device by excessive heat, voltage, or current.

example.english: The lightning managed to fry the device.
example.jyutping: bou6 gei1 bei2 leoi4 din6 siu1 waai6 zo2

rows.note: Use 熱死 when someone suffers unbearably in excessive heat, often as colloquial exaggeration.

example.english: It’s so hot today, I could fry.
example.traditional: 今日咁熱，我真係熱死喇。
example.jyutping: gam1 jat6 gam3 jit6 ngo5 zan1 hai6 jit6 sei2 laa3

rows.note: Use this pattern for a fried stick of a named non-potato food, such as 炸芝士條.

example.english: This cheese fry is really crispy.
example.traditional: 呢條炸芝士條真係好香脆。
example.jyutping: ni1 tiu4 zaa3 zi1 si2 tiu4 zan1 hai6 hou2 hoeng1 ceoi3
